newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian reshuffle almost complete this week - premier.
newsitem.headline: Russian reshuffle almost complete this week - premier.

text.p: Russia's government reshuffle will be largely completed this week, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday, adding he planned to present most of his remaining nominations to the president on Wednesday.

In remarks broadcast on television, Chernomyrdin also told reporters that federal and local authorities, and especially employers, had done "far from everything" to ensure workers received wages on time and promised the government would take "the most drastic measures" to sort out delays.

Trade unions have called on millions of workers to stage strikes and protests across the country on Thursday against the government's economic policy and, especially, long backlogs in wage and pension payments.
However, Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin may have defused some of the anger by appointing a new reform-minded cabinet led by youthful first deputy premiers Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov.
Chubais was appointed two weeks ago. Nemtsov and a number of other deputy prime ministers were named last Monday.
A number of more junior cabinet posts remain to be filled.
